insights.concise_text: The paper addresses the absence of baseline reports for Hate and Abusive Speech on Twitter by presenting reliable baseline results from the first comparative study on this dataset.

triple.subject: first comparative study on Hate and Abusive Speech on Twitter
triple.object: reliable baseline results

insights.concise_text: The paper fills the gap in studies of neural models with large-scale datasets over 100K by evaluating CNN, RNN, and their variants on Hate and Abusive Speech on Twitter.

triple.subject: CNN, RNN, and their variants
triple.object: Hate and Abusive Speech on Twitter

insights.concise_text: Because abusive language detection is context-dependent, the authors directly use text sequences of context tweets as an additional feature of neural network models.

triple.subject: context-dependent abusive language detection
triple.object: text sequences of context tweets as an additional feature of neural network models

insights.concise_text: The context-tweet feature designed to avoid data dependency yields CNN with context tweets scoring the highest recall and F1 for “hateful" labels.

triple.subject: CNN with context tweets
triple.object: highest recall and F1 for “hateful" labels

insights.concise_text: The context-tweet feature designed to avoid data dependency yields RNN models with context tweets having the highest recall for “abusive" tweets.

triple.subject: RNN models with context tweets
triple.object: highest recall for “abusive" tweets

insights.concise_text: Although HybridCNN outperformed word-level and character-level CNNs in prior abusive language detection, HybridCNN does not improve the baseline CNN model in this study.

triple.subject: HybridCNN
triple.object: no improvement over the baseline CNN model in this study

insights.concise_text: The LTC method applied to bidirectional GRU networks provides the most accurate results in detecting abusive language, while RNN with LTC modules have the highest accuracy score.

triple.subject: bidirectional GRU networks with LTC
triple.object: most accurate results in detecting abusive language

insights.concise_text: Character-level features significantly decrease classification accuracy for CNN and RNN models, which the paper attributes to lack of labeled data and significant imbalance among the different labels.

triple.subject: lack of labeled data and significant imbalance among the different labels
triple.object: reduced classification accuracy for CNN and RNN models

insights.concise_text: Character-level representations improve F1 scores of SVM and RF classifiers because traditional machine learning classifiers were trained only with the most significant character elements using TF-IDF values.

triple.subject: most significant character elements using TF-IDF values
triple.object: improved F1 scores of SVM and RF classifiers

insights.concise_text: The RNN-LTC model, a variant suffering from data insufficiency, achieves the highest F1 score for “spam" (0.551), while CNN with context tweets achieves the highest for “hateful" (0.309).

triple.subject: variant neural network models
triple.object: “spam" (0.551) and “hateful" (0.309) F1 scores
